lines.text: It's late. You open your bank app, and there it is. A charge you don't recognize.
You report it. And then, you wait.
At this bank, the median wait for a first answer is thirty-seven hours.
I wanted that answer in seconds. And I wanted it to be right.
So I built the LATAM Bank Dispute Agent.
The customer writes it in their own words. The agent finds the exact charge in their history, and asks: is this the one?
One short explanation, and it's done. A provisional credit, the card blocked, a reference number. Every fact is checked against the record.
Charged twice for one taxi? It doesn't guess. It shows the customer their own charges, and lets them pick.
Then it finds the twin in the data, and refunds one. Only one.
And when a charge should not be paid automatically, it knows not to act.
It asks the questions an advisor would call back for. Then a person gets the full case file: verified facts, the customer's story, and what is still open.
Why would a bank trust it? Because the model only reads. The rules and permissions live in code. And every fact is checked against the customer's own ledger.
I built it on a focused slice of the data: one month of transactions. A dispute only needs recent history, and the live app never touches the raw data.
